title: The Halvorsen Library
intro: You wake up slumped over a reading table in a dim, silent library. Candles flicker. The only exit is a heavy iron-banded door with a four-digit keypad. Somewhere in this room is the way out. (Type 'help' for commands or 'hint' if you get stuck.)
room_description: A small, candle-lit reading room with dark wood panelling and the smell of old paper.

desk.name: oak desk
desk.description: A heavy oak writing desk covered in dust. A narrow drawer is built into its front, held shut by a small brass dial.

drawer.name: desk drawer
drawer.description: A narrow drawer in the front of the oak desk.

lock.locked_text: It is held shut by a brass dial with three number wheels.
lock.gate_message: You spin the dial at random, but you would only be guessing — you have not found anything that hints at the combination yet.
lock.wrong_message: You set the dial and pull. The drawer does not budge — wrong combination.
lock.success_message: The dial clicks into place at 7-1-4 and the drawer slides open.

bookshelf.name: bookshelf
bookshelf.description: A towering bookshelf of leather-bound volumes. Three books stand out because each has a single gold number stamped on its spine. From left to right: a blue book marked 4, a red book marked 7 and a green book marked 1.

painting.name: painting
painting.description: An oil portrait of a stern woman in a high collar. A tarnished plate reads 'Edda Halvorsen, Founder'. Parts of the dark background have an odd, glossy sheen, as if something was painted over.

reveal.text: Glowing letters are still faintly visible across the background: M D C C C X L V I I.

globe.name: antique globe
globe.description: A large antique globe on a wooden stand. A thin seam runs around its equator.

lock.locked_text: There is a small brass keyhole near the North Pole; the two halves are locked together.
lock.success_message: The brass key turns with a satisfying click and the upper half of the globe hinges open.

door.name: exit door
door.description: A heavy iron-banded door — the only way out.

lock.locked_text: A four-digit keypad is mounted beside the handle. The door is locked.
lock.gate_message: You punch in a few digits, but you would only be guessing — you have not found the door's clue yet.
lock.wrong_message: The keypad buzzes and flashes red. Wrong code.
lock.success_message: The keypad flashes green — 1-8-4-7. Bolts slide back and the door swings open. Cool night air rushes in. You have escaped!

note.name: folded note
note.description: A note in faded ink: 'My books are shelved out of order — open the drawer in the order of the rainbow.'

brass_key.name: brass key
brass_key.description: A small, ornate brass key. Its bow is shaped like a tiny globe.

uv_lamp.name: UV lamp
uv_lamp.description: A pocket ultraviolet lamp. It casts a faint violet glow when switched on.

use_rules.message: You switch on the UV lamp and sweep it across the portrait. Glowing letters appear across the dark background: M D C C C X L V I I.
use_rules.repeat_message: Under the violet light the letters glow again: M D C C C X L V I I.

puzzles.label: UV lamp → hidden message in the painting

hints.text: Start with the desk — someone left something on it.
The note talks about books. Take a closer look at the bookshelf.
Put the book numbers in the order the note describes (think of a rainbow) and try that on the desk drawer.
The drawer is open — check what is inside.
That key needs a keyhole. Have you examined the globe?
Something is waiting inside the open globe.
Ultraviolet light shows what ordinary eyes miss. Try it on the painting.
The glowing letters are Roman numerals. Convert them into a four-digit number for the door keypad.
